steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Stinky Steve and the Missing Sock
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
Once upon a time, in the back of a sock drawer, there lived a very stinky sock named Steve.

Steve wasn't like the other socks. While they smelled like lavender and fresh laundry, Steve smelled like... well, Steve.

"Has anyone seen my match?" Steve called out one laundry day.

All the other socks backed away slowly.

"Maybe check the gym bag," squeaked a little ankle sock.

So Steve went to the gym bag. And there — tangled up with a sweaty headband and three granola bar wrappers — was his missing match.

"STEVE JR!" he cried.

Steve Jr. was even stinkier than Steve.

Together, they were unstoppable.

The end. 🧦

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Stinky Steve and the Sock Showdown
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
It was Saturday morning, and all the socks were arguing.

"I'm the comfiest!" bragged the fuzzy purple one.
"I'm the fastest!" shouted the neon running sock.
"I'm the fanciest!" said the sparkly gold sock, flipping her cuff dramatically.

Then Stinky Steve yawned from the corner. "I'm the stinkiest," he said proudly.

Everyone groaned.

"That's not something to brag about, Steve!"

But Steve grinned. "Oh yeah? Let's have a contest! The Great Sock Showdown!"

So they did.

Round one was the Stretch Test. Steve gave it his all… and accidentally slingshotted himself straight into a pile of clean laundry. "Ten points for style!" yelled a baby sock.

Round two was the Slide Race across the hardwood floor. They zoomed off — but Steve's stink left such a strong trail that the others started slipping and spinning out. Steve crossed the finish line sideways, yelling, "Victory stinks!"

The final round was the Sniff Test. The cat sniffed the first sock. Purr. The second sock. Purr. Then it got to Steve… and ran away so fast its tail puffed up like a balloon!

All the socks burst out laughing. Even the fancy gold one fell over giggling.

"Okay, okay," she said. "You win, Steve. You're officially the funniest and smelliest sock in the drawer."

Steve took a bow. "I'd like to thank the gym shoes, the laundry basket, and of course, my nose."

The end. 🧦🏆😂

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Cub the Grizzly
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
Deep in the forest, under tall pine trees and big snowy mountains, lived a little grizzly bear named Cub.

Cub was strong. Cub was fast. And Cub loved to play rough. He liked to tumble, roll, and pounce in the grass.

"RAWR!" Cub would say as he jumped onto his friend Moose. Moose wobbled and laughed. "Cub! You're a rough player!"

Cub didn't mean to be rough. He was just excited.

One day Cub saw Bunny hopping through the meadow. "Let's play!" said Cub.

Cub pounced. Boop! Bunny rolled over in the soft grass.

"Cub!" Bunny giggled. "You're a little too strong!"

Cub's ears drooped. "I just want to play," he said quietly.

Old Mama Bear watched from under a big tree. She walked over and gave Cub a warm bear hug.

"Cub," she said gently, "you have a big grizzly body and a big grizzly heart. You just need to remember to use gentle paws with small friends."

Cub thought about that.

The next day he saw Bunny again. "Want to play?" asked Cub.

"Okay!" said Bunny.

Cub tiptoed closer. Instead of pouncing, he rolled softly beside Bunny. They tumbled in the grass. They laughed. They chased butterflies.

And when Moose came by, Cub gave him a big rough bear wrestle. Moose loved it. Because Moose was big enough.

That night Cub curled up in his cozy den. Mama Bear tucked him in.

"You played well today," she whispered.

Cub yawned a big grizzly yawn. "I'm a rough bear," he said sleepily.

"Yes," Mama Bear smiled. "But you're also a kind bear."

Cub closed his eyes. The forest grew quiet. The moon glowed over the mountains. And little Cub the grizzly dreamed of tumbling, playing, and using his gentle paws.

Goodnight, Cub. Goodnight, forest. 🌙🐻

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Cub and the Big Forest Game
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
In a wide green forest, under tall trees and bright stars, lived a little grizzly bear named Cub.

Cub loved to run, climb, and wrestle. He was very strong for a little bear. Sometimes when Cub played, he would tumble so hard that whoosh! everyone would roll over. But Cub was a very nice bear.

One morning Cub woke up early. The sun peeked through the trees. "Today is a perfect day to play!" Cub said.

He ran to the meadow where his friends were. Bunny was hopping. Squirrel was climbing. Moose was munching grass.

"Let's play the Big Forest Game!" said Cub.

"What's that?" asked Squirrel.

"It's a game where we run, hide, and chase!" said Cub excitedly.

"Okay!" said everyone.

"Ready… set… GO!"

Cub ran fast. Too fast! He zoomed past Bunny and made the grass whoosh. Bunny tumbled over.

"Oh!" said Cub, stopping quickly. "Sorry Bunny. I forgot my gentle paws."

Bunny stood up and shook the grass off. "That's okay," she said. "You're just a big, strong bear."

Cub thought for a moment. Then he had an idea.

"I'll be the tree guard," Cub said. "I'll stay by the big tree and tag anyone who runs by!"

The friends loved that idea. They ran around the meadow. Squirrel zipped past the tree. Tag! Cub gently tapped him. Moose trotted by. Cub gave him a playful nudge. And Bunny hopped right between Cub's paws.

Everyone laughed and laughed.

When the sun started to go down, the friends lay in the grass together.

"That was the best game," said Bunny.

"Yeah," said Squirrel.

Moose nodded. "Cub is the best tree guard."

Cub smiled a big grizzly smile. He liked playing rough. But he liked being a good friend even more.

That night Cub snuggled into his cozy den. Mama Bear tucked him in.

"Did you have a good day?" she asked.

Cub yawned. "The best," he said softly.

Outside, the forest grew quiet. The stars twinkled. And little Cub the grizzly fell asleep dreaming of running, playing, and all his forest friends.

Goodnight, Cub. 🌙🐻

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Benny the Beaver Meets Cub the Friendly Grizzly
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
One golden afternoon, Benny the Beaver, Milly the Mouse, and Oliver the Otter were playing near the forest’s edge.

“I wonder what’s past those trees,” Oliver said, pointing to a path they had never taken before.

Milly’s whiskers twitched. “It looks a little… big.”

Benny smiled. “Let’s go together.”

So the three friends walked down the new path.

The trees grew taller.
The shadows grew longer.

And then…

CRUNCH… CRACK… THUMP!

Something big was coming.

Milly squeaked and hid behind Benny.
Oliver froze in the water.

Out from the bushes stepped a large, furry bear.

But he didn’t look scary.

He looked… sad.

“Hi,” the bear said softly. “I’m Cub.”

Benny blinked. “Hi… I’m Benny.”

“I didn’t mean to scare you,” Cub said, looking down. “I just… I was trying to play, but I’m too big. I always break things.”

Just then, Cub took a step forward—

CRACK!

A small pile of sticks broke under his paw.

Cub sighed. “See?”

Milly peeked out. “You’re not scary… just a little clumsy.”

Oliver nodded. “And really big.”

Cub gave a tiny smile.

Benny thought for a moment.

Then he said, “Maybe you don’t need to play smaller… maybe we just need to build something stronger.”

Cub’s eyes lit up. “Really?”

“Really,” Benny said.

So they got to work.

Benny found the strongest logs.

Oliver rolled heavy branches into place.

Milly tucked in little sticks to hold it together.

And Cub?

Cub carried the biggest logs of all.

Together they built a super strong play area — with a wide slide, a sturdy bridge, and even a giant splash spot.

“Try it!” said Benny.

Cub climbed up carefully.

He took a deep breath.

Then…

WHEEEE!

Down he slid—

SPLOOOOSH!

Water splashed everywhere!

The friends burst out laughing.

“It didn’t break!” Cub said, amazed.

“Because we built it together,” Benny said.

Cub smiled the biggest smile of all.

For the rest of the afternoon, they played and laughed and splashed.

And when the sun began to set, Cub said softly,

“Thanks for not being scared of me.”

Milly smiled. “Thanks for being our friend.”

Benny added, “Everyone has something special to bring.”

Oliver splashed. “Yours is being big and strong!”

Cub beamed.

As the sky turned dark and stars began to twinkle, the new friends said goodnight.

And in the quiet forest, with happy hearts and tired paws…

Everyone drifted off to sleep.

The End. 🌙

Little lesson: Being different is what makes you special — and kindness helps everyone belong. 💛

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Benny the Beaver Meets Tigger
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
One sunny morning, Benny the Beaver, Milly the Mouse, Oliver the Otter, and Cub the friendly grizzly were playing by the river.

“I built a new bouncing bridge!” Benny said proudly.

“A bouncing bridge?!” Oliver laughed. “That sounds fun!”

Just then—

BOUNCE! BOING! BOUNCE-BOUNCE-BOUNCE!

Something orange came springing through the trees.

“Helloooooo!” he sang.

It was Tigger!

“I’m Tigger! T-I-double-guh-er!” he cheered, bouncing on his tail.

Milly’s eyes went wide. “He’s very… bouncy.”

Cub blinked. “Very, very bouncy.”

Tigger bounced right onto Benny’s new bridge.

“Let’s try it out!” he said.

BOING!

The bridge bounced.

BOING-BOING!

The logs wiggled.

BOOOOING!

“Uh oh…” said Benny.

CRACK! SPLASH!

The bridge fell into the water!

Everyone went quiet.

Tigger stopped bouncing.

“Oh dear,” he said softly. “Did I break it?”

Benny looked at the broken bridge. He felt a little upset… he had worked hard on it.

But then he took a deep breath.

“It’s okay,” Benny said. “It was made for gentle steps… not super bounces.”

Tigger’s ears drooped. “I didn’t mean to. I just get so excited.”

Milly stepped forward. “You didn’t know.”

Oliver nodded. “And you said sorry.”

Cub added, “We can fix it together!”

Tigger’s face lit up. “Really?! I LOVE helping!”

So they all got to work.

Benny planned a stronger bridge.

Cub carried giant logs.

Oliver pushed them into place.

Milly tucked tiny sticks in the cracks.

And Tigger?

He bounced carefully this time… carrying vines and leaves to tie everything together.

Soon, the new bridge was ready.

“Let’s test it,” said Benny.

Everyone walked across slowly.

Step… step… step…

The bridge stayed strong.

Tigger looked at his tail.

“Maybe I try a tiny bounce?” he said.

“Tiny,” Benny agreed.

Tigger did the smallest bounce ever.

Boop!

The bridge didn’t move.

Everyone cheered!

Tigger laughed. “I can still be bouncy AND careful!”

Benny smiled. “And that’s what makes a great friend.”

As the sun set, they all sat on the bridge together.

Even Tigger stayed (mostly) still.

And in the quiet, happy forest…

Everyone felt proud, kind, and ready for sleep.

The End. 🌙

Little lesson: It’s okay to be yourself—but being kind means thinking about how your actions affect others. 💛

rush-stories.title: Luma and Ember
rush-stories.body:
Once upon a time, in a quiet forest filled with glowing flowers and whispering trees, there lived a tiny fairy named Luma.

Luma had soft, shimmering wings and a curious heart. Every night, she would fly through the forest, sprinkling a little sparkle wherever things looked dull or sleepy.

One evening, as the sun tucked itself behind the mountains, Luma heard a deep rumble.

"Hmm," she said, tilting her head. "That doesn't sound like a sleepy bunny… or a snoring owl."

She followed the sound past the twinkling stream, over mossy rocks, and into a part of the forest she had never visited before.

There, curled up beside a big, warm rock, was a dragon.

He was HUGE. With shiny green scales, gentle golden eyes, and a long tail wrapped around his feet. But instead of looking scary… he looked sad.

"Hello?" Luma said softly, hovering nearby.

The dragon blinked slowly. "Oh! Hello, little fairy," he said in a deep but kind voice. "I didn't mean to scare you."

"I'm not scared," Luma said bravely. "Why are you so sad?"

The dragon sighed, and a tiny puff of warm air floated into the sky. "My name is Ember. I try to be gentle, but whenever I get lonely, I accidentally let out big rumbles and puffs of fire… and everyone runs away."

Luma thought for a moment, then smiled. "Maybe you just need a friend who understands."

Ember's eyes lit up a little. "You'd really be my friend? Even if I'm big and loud?"

"Of course," Luma said. "And maybe… we can practice being calm together."

So they tried.

Luma showed Ember how to take slow, quiet breaths. In… and out…

Each time Ember breathed out, instead of a big flame—just a tiny, warm sparkle appeared.

"Oh!" Ember said, surprised. "Did you do that?"

Luma giggled. "Maybe a little magic… and a lot of calm."

Soon, Ember's rumbles turned into soft hums, like a cozy song. The forest animals peeked out from behind trees and bushes, curious instead of scared.

A bunny hopped closer. Then a deer. Even the owls fluttered down to watch.

"You see?" Luma said. "You're not scary. You're just… big and wonderful."

Ember smiled the biggest, warmest smile.

"Thank you, Luma," he said. "I don't feel lonely anymore."

From that night on, the fairy and the dragon met every evening. Luma would sprinkle gentle sparkles, and Ember would glow softly like a warm lantern in the dark.

And the forest? It felt safer, cozier, and a little more magical than ever before.

The end. 🌙✨

steph-custom-recipes.name: Lemon Yogurt Chicken
steph-custom-recipes.desc: The Modern Nonna · Greek-inspired · Super juicy thighs · Yogurt marinade · 45–60 min · 4.65 stars
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Serves 4 | Marinate 1 hr – overnight | Bake 45–60 min at 400F (200C)

INGREDIENTS:
• 4–6 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs
• 3/4 cup plain Greek or Balkan-style yogurt
• 2 lemons (juice + keep the squeezed halves)
• 6 garlic cloves
• 2 tbsp olive oil
• 1 tsp dried oregano
• Salt and black pepper to taste

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Add chicken to a baking dish with olive oil and yogurt.
2. Season with salt, pepper, and oregano.
3. Squeeze in the juice of both lemons, then add the squeezed lemon pieces to the dish.
4. Add garlic cloves.
5. Massage everything together with clean hands.
6. Marinate in the fridge at least 1 hour, or overnight.
7. Bake uncovered 45–60 min at 400F until 165F internal temp.
8. Optional: broil 1–2 min to crisp the skin.

NOTE: Yogurt tenderizes and keeps chicken incredibly juicy. Balkan, Bulgarian, or Greek yogurt all work.

steph-custom-recipes.name: Caramelized Onion Pasta
steph-custom-recipes.desc: The Modern Nonna · Oven-caramelized onions + Boursin · Bowtie pasta · 4.86 stars · 75 min
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Serves 4 | Oven time 60–70 min | Total ~80 min

INGREDIENTS:
• 3–4 large yellow onions, thinly sliced
• 1 whole head of garlic
• 1 tbsp balsamic glaze
• 3 tbsp olive oil (+ a drizzle for garlic)
• 1/2 cup sun-dried tomatoes
• 1 tsp Italian seasoning
• 1 package (150g) Boursin cheese (garlic & herb)
• 300g bowtie (farfalle) pasta
• 1/2 cup reserved pasta water
• Fresh basil, Parmesan, chili oil to garnish

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Preheat oven to 400F (200C).
2. In a large baking dish, combine sliced onions, balsamic glaze, olive oil, sun-dried tomatoes, and Italian seasoning. Mix well.
3. Cut the top off the garlic head to expose cloves, drizzle with olive oil, and place in the center of the dish.
4. Bake 60–70 min, stirring 2–3 times, until onions are deeply caramelized.
5. About 10 min before onions are done, cook pasta per package instructions. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.
6. Squeeze the roasted garlic directly into the onion mixture. Add Boursin and stir to combine.
7. Add hot pasta and splash of pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce.
8. Toss well. Garnish with fresh basil, Parmesan, and chili oil if desired.

NOTE: The pasta water is key — the starch helps the sauce coat every piece. Don't skip it. Leftovers hold up great for lunch the next day.

steph-custom-recipes.name: Hamburger Helper (Homemade)
steph-custom-recipes.desc: The Modern Nonna · Ground beef + pasta + cheddar · One pot · 30 min · 4.63 stars
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Serves 4 | 30 min | One pot

INGREDIENTS:
• 500g ground beef (or turkey, pork, chicken)
• 1 tbsp olive oil
• 1 small onion, diced
• 3 garlic cloves, minced
• 2 tbsp tomato paste
• 1 tsp paprika
• 1 tsp garlic powder
• 1 tsp onion powder
• Salt and pepper to taste
• 2 cups beef or bone broth (unsalted or low sodium)
• 1.5 cups water
• 2 cups small pasta (elbow macaroni or small shells)
• 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high. Add ground beef, breaking apart and cooking until water evaporates and meat browns.
2. Add onion and stir. Add garlic and stir.
3. Add tomato paste and all seasonings. Stir to coat.
4. Pour in broth and water. Add pasta.
5. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring every few minutes to prevent sticking, until pasta is cooked through (8–10 min).
6. Remove from heat, stir in cheddar until melted.
7. Serve immediately.

NOTE: Keep stirring once pasta goes in — it will stick to the bottom if left alone. Freezes beautifully. Rush-friendly — mild flavour, cheesy pasta with meat.

steph-custom-recipes.name: High Protein Mini Pancakes (Viral)
steph-custom-recipes.desc: The Modern Nonna · 2 ingredients · ~30g protein · under 200 cal · 10 min · Breakfast
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Serves 1 | 10 min | ~200 cal · ~30g protein

INGREDIENTS:
• 1 cup liquid egg whites (or whites from ~8 large eggs)
• 1 tsp vanilla bean paste (optional but recommended)
• Pinch of cream of tartar or a few drops of lemon juice (helps stabilize)
• Optional: 1 scoop protein powder, folded in gently after peaks form

TOPPINGS (optional):
• Fresh berries, maple syrup, powdered sugar

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Add egg whites to a clean bowl. Add cream of tartar or lemon juice.
2. Whip with a hand or stand mixer until stiff peaks form.
3. Gently fold in vanilla bean paste (and protein powder if using) — do not overmix or they'll deflate.
4. Spoon into a silicone muffin pan or drop scoops onto a parchment-lined baking sheet.
5. Bake at 375F (190C) for 8–10 min until lightly golden.
6. Top with berries, powdered sugar, or maple syrup and serve immediately.

NOTE: Texture is like a cross between a meringue and a soufflé — cloud-like and melt-in-your-mouth. Use pure liquid egg whites with no additives or they won't whip. Don't deflate the peaks — fold gently. Eat right away, they don't hold long.

steph-custom-recipes.name: Big Mac Smash Tacos
steph-custom-recipes.desc: The Modern Nonna · Smash burger on a tortilla + homemade Mac Sauce · 20 min · 4.65 stars
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Makes 5 tacos | 20 min

MAC SAUCE:
• 3 tbsp mayo
• 1 tbsp sour cream
• 1 tbsp plain yogurt
• 1 tsp tomato paste
• 1 tsp honey Dijon mustard
• 1 tbsp sweet relish
• 1 tsp pickle juice
Stir together and refrigerate until ready.

TACOS:
• 500g ground beef
• 5 small flour tortillas
• Salt and pepper
• Avocado oil or spray
• 5 slices American or cheddar cheese
• Shredded iceberg lettuce
• Finely chopped white onion
• Pickles, sliced

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Make the Mac Sauce — stir all sauce ingredients together, set aside.
2. Divide ground beef into 5 equal balls.
3. Press each ball flat onto a small flour tortilla in a thin even layer. Season with salt and pepper.
4. Heat pan on medium-high with a touch of avocado oil.
5. Place tortilla meat-side down. Cook 2–3 min until golden and caramelized.
6. Flip, add a slice of cheese, reduce to medium-low, put lid on until cheese melts.
7. Remove from heat. Top with lettuce, onion, pickles, and a drizzle of Mac Sauce.
8. Serve immediately.

NOTE: Rush-friendly — skip the Mac sauce and pickles for his, just plain meat + cheese on tortilla. Double the recipe — they go fast.

steph-custom-recipes.name: Ricotta Gnocchi
steph-custom-recipes.desc: Pasta Social Club · 2-ingredient pasta dough · Serves 2 · 30 min
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Serves 2 | ~30 min

INGREDIENTS:
• 1½ cups (340g) very firm and/or drained whole milk ricotta
• 1 cup (125g) '00' or all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
• ⅓ cup (45g) Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated
• ~½ tsp kosher salt
• 1 whole egg + 1 egg yolk, beaten together
• Dash of freshly grated nutmeg (optional)

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. If ricotta is watery, drain in a cheesecloth-lined colander over a bowl in the fridge for ~1 hour. Or spread on a paper-towel-lined plate to absorb excess liquid.
2. Add dry ricotta to a medium mixing bowl. Add egg mixture and stir to combine. Stir in parmesan.
3. In a separate bowl, combine salt and flour. Add to cheese mixture along with nutmeg. Fold in gently until just incorporated. Form into a ball (it'll be sticky).
4. Cut dough into 8 wedges on a wooden board. Dust each with flour and roll into a rope, about ¾ inch thick. Cut into pillows of desired size.
5. Place finished gnocchi on a parchment-lined baking sheet dusted with flour.
6. Boil in well-salted water until they float. Finish in your desired sauce for 1–2 minutes. Serve immediately.

NOTE: Serve with brown butter and sage, marinara, or any light cream sauce. Rush-friendly with simple butter sauce.

steph-custom-recipes.name: Pantry Pomodoro Sauce
steph-custom-recipes.desc: Pasta Social Club · Simple tomato butter sauce · 20 min
steph-custom-recipes.body:
PANTRY POMODORO SAUCE | ~20 min | Serves 4

INGREDIENTS:
• 4 garlic cloves, minced
• 1 pint fresh cherry tomatoes, halved (optional)
• 1½ cups tomato passata/puree or finely chopped tomatoes (increase to 2–3 cups if not using fresh tomatoes)
• 6 tbsp butter
• Salt and pepper to taste

OPTIONAL ADD-INS:
• Fresh or fried capers
• Toasted panko breadcrumbs (seasoned with salt and/or Parmigiano-Reggiano)
• Pecorino Romano cheese
• Crushed Calabrian chili peppers or red pepper flakes
• Tinned tuna in olive oil
• Anchovies (dissolve in butter before adding garlic)
• Fresh herbs

METHOD:
1. Toss cherry tomatoes with kosher salt in a bowl and marinate 30 minutes at room temperature.
2. In a medium sauté pan with lid, cook garlic in 2 tbsp butter over medium heat until fragrant, ~1 minute (watch closely!).
3. Add salted cherry tomatoes (with their juices) and tomato passata. Stir to combine.
4. [Optional: add tinned tuna, capers + brine, and red pepper flakes for puttanesca-style sauce. Break tuna into pieces.]
5. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat until tomatoes break down and puree caramelizes, 10–15 minutes. Stir occasionally.
6. Finish with remaining 4 tbsp butter. Adjust seasoning.
7. Serve with pasta (add pasta water to sauce), topped with any of the above garnishes.

NOTES: Use fresh cherry tomatoes when in season. Can be made all-pantry with canned tomatoes. Works as a base for other dishes.

steph-custom-recipes.name: Montana's Antojitos (Copycat)
steph-custom-recipes.desc: The Cookie Writer · Canadian classic copycat · Cheesy rolled tortilla appetizer · 35 min · Makes 20
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Makes 20 pieces | Prep 15 min | Bake 20 min at 375F

INGREDIENTS:
• 5 large tortillas
• 1 cup cream cheese, room temperature
• ½ cup cheddar cheese, grated
• ½ red pepper, finely diced
• ½ green pepper, finely diced
• 1–2 jalapeños, finely diced
• 3 green onions, finely diced
• Salt & pepper
• ¼ tsp dried oregano (optional)
• ¼ tsp garlic powder (optional)

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Finely dice all veggies (food processor works — don't over-blend; drain if wet)
2. Mix cream cheese, cheddar, veggies, and seasonings
3. Spread filling onto tortillas and roll up tightly
4. Slice into rounds (~4 per tortilla)
5. Bake at 375F for ~20 min until golden

NOTES:
• Not spicy despite jalapeños
• Drain veggie mixture before mixing with cheese
• Gluten-free: use corn tortillas
• More cheese = more "greasy" (leaks out more)

steph-custom-recipes.name: Jennifer Aniston Mason Jar Salad
steph-custom-recipes.desc: PlantYou · Quinoa, chickpeas, cucumber, fresh herbs, pistachios · Light lemon vinaigrette · 35 min · Serves 4
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Serves 4 | Prep 20 min | Cook 15 min | Keeps 4 days in fridge

DRESSING (Light Lemon Vinaigrette):
• ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil
• 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice
• 1 tsp maple syrup
• ½ tsp Dijon mustard
• Salt and pepper to taste

SALAD:
• 1 cup dry quinoa
• 1 (14oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
• ½ cup finely diced red onion
• 1½ cups diced cucumber
• ⅓ cup chopped fresh parsley
• ⅓ cup chopped fresh mint
• ⅓ cup crumbled vegan feta
• ¼ cup roasted pistachios, roughly chopped
• ¼ cup finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes (optional)

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Rinse quinoa, cook in 2 cups water with pinch of salt for 12-15 min. Cool completely.
2. Whisk dressing ingredients together.
3. Layer in 4 x 32oz mason jars: dressing → chickpeas → red onion → cucumber → sun-dried tomatoes → quinoa → parsley & mint → feta → pistachios
4. Seal and refrigerate up to 4 days.

SERVE: Shake well and pour into a bowl. Finish with extra lemon and black pepper.

4. Seal and refrigerate up to 3 days.

SERVE: Add extra pepper or chili flakes when ready to eat.

steph-custom-recipes.body:

PEANUT SAUCE:
• ½ cup natural peanut butter
• 3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
• 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
• 1 tbsp rice vinegar
• 1 tbsp maple syrup
• 1 tsp sesame oil
• 1-3 tbsp warm water (to thin)
• 1 small garlic clove, finely minced
• ½ tsp freshly grated ginger

• 7oz dry ramen noodles
• 1 cup shelled edamame (frozen and thawed)
• 2 cups finely shredded red cabbage

5. Seal and refrigerate up to 3 days.

• ½ cup thinly sliced red onion
• ⅓ cup chopped fresh cilantro
• ½ cup crumbled feta cheese
• 2 tbsp olive oil (for corn)

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Cook macaroni al dente, drain and rinse under cold water. Cool completely.
2. Toss corn with olive oil, cook in skillet on medium-high 5-7 min until lightly charred. Season with salt. Cool completely.
3. Whisk dressing ingredients together, adding water gradually until smooth and pourable.
4. Layer in 4 x 32oz mason jars: yogurt dressing → corn → feta → sliced red onions → pasta → cilantro
5. Seal and refrigerate up to 3 days.

SERVE: Shake, pour into bowl. Add lime wedge and chili flakes or hot sauce.

steph-custom-recipes.name: Farmhouse Sandwich Bread
steph-custom-recipes.desc: @healthyhomesteader · Simple everyday sandwich loaf · Soft & fluffy · 2 hr total · Viral recipe
steph-custom-recipes.body:
Serves: 1 loaf | Total time: ~2 hrs (including rise time) | Bake: 375°F for 25–30 min

INGREDIENTS:
• 3 cups flour
• 1 cup warm milk
• 2 tbsp butter
• 1 egg
• 2¼ tsp yeast
• 1 tbsp honey
• 1 tsp salt

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Combine warm milk, honey and yeast — let sit 5 min until foamy
2. Add butter, egg, salt and flour
3. Mix and knead until soft and smooth (8–10 min by hand or stand mixer)
4. Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled
5. Punch down, shape into a loaf and place in greased loaf pan
6. Rise again 30–45 min
7. Bake at 375°F for 25–30 min until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped

NOTE: Perfect recipe to try with freshly milled soft white wheat berries.

Source: @colleenshealthylife

• Place on parchment paper and freeze 5 min until firm

THE ICE CREAM (Ninja Creami chocolate protein):
• 1 can lite coconut milk
• 1 heaping scoop chocolate protein powder (dairy-free bone broth protein recommended)
• 1 heaping scoop collagen (keeps it creamy)
• 1/2 tbsp cocoa powder
• 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
• 1/2 tsp vanilla extract

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Blend all ice cream ingredients until smooth
2. Freeze 24 hours in Creami pint
3. Run on Lite Ice Cream setting
4. Add a splash of milk if needed and re-spin for perfect creaminess
5. Sandwich ice cream between two frozen cherry "cookies"
6. Enjoy immediately!

NOTE: Can use any favourite chocolate ice cream instead of making the Creami version.

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Stinky Steve and the Missing Sock
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
Once upon a time, in the back of a sock drawer, there lived a very stinky sock named Steve.

Steve wasn't like the other socks. While they smelled like lavender and fresh laundry, Steve smelled like... well, Steve.

"Has anyone seen my match?" Steve called out one laundry day.

All the other socks backed away slowly.

"Maybe check the gym bag," squeaked a little ankle sock.

So Steve went to the gym bag. And there — tangled up with a sweaty headband and three granola bar wrappers — was his missing match.

"STEVE JR!" he cried.

Steve Jr. was even stinkier than Steve.

Together, they were unstoppable.

The end. 🧦

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Stinky Steve and the Sock Showdown
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
It was Saturday morning, and all the socks were arguing.

"I'm the comfiest!" bragged the fuzzy purple one.
"I'm the fastest!" shouted the neon running sock.
"I'm the fanciest!" said the sparkly gold sock, flipping her cuff dramatically.

Then Stinky Steve yawned from the corner. "I'm the stinkiest," he said proudly.

Everyone groaned. "That's not something to brag about, Steve!"

But Steve grinned. "Oh yeah? Let's have a contest! The Great Sock Showdown!"

Round one: Stretch Test. Steve accidentally slingshotted himself into clean laundry. "Ten points for style!"

Round two: Slide Race. Steve's stink left such a strong trail the others spun out. Steve crossed the finish line sideways yelling, "Victory stinks!"

The Sniff Test: the cat sniffed the first sock — Purr. Second sock — Purr. Steve... and ran away so fast its tail puffed up like a balloon!

All the socks burst out laughing.

"You win, Steve. You're officially the funniest and smelliest sock in the drawer."

Steve took a bow.

The end. 🧦🏆😂

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Stinky Steve and the Sock Olympics
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
Stinky Steve wasn't just any sock — he was the stinkiest sock in the drawer.
He had survived soccer practice, playground puddles, and one very suspicious spaghetti dinner.

One night, when everyone was asleep, the sock drawer came alive!
"Tonight," said Steve proudly, "we're holding the first-ever Sock Olympics!"

Races, high jumps, and a competition for "Most Stretchy."

Steve sprinted across the dresser, leapt over a shoelace, and stuck the landing (mostly). "Ta-da!"

But when it came to the Sniff Test event, everyone took one whiff of Steve and fainted dramatically. Even the sock referee rolled over.

Steve sniffed himself and laughed so hard he fell off the drawer.
"I guess I am the champion!"

The next morning, the human picked him up with two fingers and tossed him in the wash.
Steve sighed happily. "Even champions need a bath."

The end. 🏅

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Cub the Grizzly
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
Deep in the forest, under tall pine trees and big snowy mountains, lived a little grizzly bear named Cub.

Cub was strong. Cub was fast. And Cub loved to play rough.

"RAWR!" Cub would say as he jumped onto his friend Moose. "Cub! You're a rough player!"

One day Cub pounced on Bunny. Boop! Bunny rolled over.

"Cub! You're a little too strong!"

Cub's ears drooped. "I just want to play."

Mama Bear walked over and gave Cub a warm hug.

"You have a big grizzly body and a big grizzly heart. Just remember to use gentle paws with small friends."

The next day, Cub tiptoed to Bunny. Instead of pouncing, he rolled softly beside her. They tumbled, laughed, and chased butterflies.

When Moose came by, Cub gave him a big rough bear wrestle. Moose loved it. Because Moose was big enough.

That night Mama Bear tucked Cub in.

"I'm a rough bear," Cub said sleepily.
"Yes," Mama Bear smiled. "But you're also a kind bear."

Goodnight, Cub. 🌙🐻

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Cub and the Big Forest Game
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
In a wide green forest, lived a little grizzly bear named Cub who loved to run, climb, and wrestle.

One morning he ran to the meadow. "Let's play the Big Forest Game!"

Cub ran fast. Too fast! He zoomed past Bunny — whoosh — Bunny tumbled over.

"Oh! Sorry Bunny. I forgot my gentle paws."

Then Cub had an idea. "I'll be the tree guard! I'll stay by the big tree and tag anyone who runs by!"

Everyone loved that. Squirrel zipped past — Tag! Moose trotted by — nudge! Bunny hopped right between Cub's paws.

Everyone laughed and laughed.

That night Mama Bear tucked Cub in. "Did you have a good day?"

Cub yawned. "The best."

Goodnight, Cub. 🌙🐻

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Benny the Beaver Meets Cub the Friendly Grizzly
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
One golden afternoon, Benny the Beaver, Milly the Mouse, and Oliver the Otter were exploring near the forest's edge when — CRUNCH… CRACK… THUMP!

Out from the bushes stepped a large, furry bear. But he didn't look scary. He looked… sad.

"Hi. I'm Cub. I was trying to play, but I'm too big. I always break things."

Benny said, "Maybe we just need to build something stronger."

So they built a super strong play area together — a wide slide, a sturdy bridge, a giant splash spot.

Cub climbed up carefully. Then— WHEEEEE! SPLOOOOSH!

"It didn't break!" Cub said, amazed.

"Because we built it together."

"Thanks for not being scared of me."

"Thanks for being our friend."

The End. 🌙

Little lesson: Being different is what makes you special — and kindness helps everyone belong. 💛

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Benny the Beaver Meets Tigger
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
"I built a new bouncing bridge!" Benny said proudly one sunny morning.

BOUNCE! BOING! Something orange came springing through the trees. It was Tigger!

Tigger bounced onto Benny's new bridge — BOING-BOING-CRACK! SPLASH! The bridge fell into the water.

"Oh dear. Did I break it?"

Benny took a deep breath. "It was made for gentle steps… not super bounces."

"I didn't mean to. I just get so excited."

"We can fix it together!" said Cub.

So they built a stronger bridge — Benny planned, Cub carried logs, Oliver pushed, Milly tucked sticks, Tigger carefully carried vines.

Tigger did the smallest bounce ever. Boop! It didn't move.

Everyone cheered! "I can still be bouncy AND careful!"

The End. 🌙

Little lesson: It's okay to be yourself — but being kind means thinking about how your actions affect others. 💛

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Luma and Ember
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
Once upon a time, in a quiet forest filled with glowing flowers and whispering trees, there lived a tiny fairy named Luma.

Luma had soft, shimmering wings and a curious heart. Every night she sprinkled sparkles wherever things looked dull or sleepy.

One evening she followed a deep rumble into a part of the forest she'd never visited — and found a huge dragon curled beside a warm rock. He had shiny green scales and gentle golden eyes. But instead of looking scary… he looked sad.

"My name is Ember. Whenever I get lonely I accidentally let out big rumbles and puffs of fire… and everyone runs away."

"Maybe you just need a friend who understands," Luma said.

So they practiced slow, quiet breaths together. In… and out… Each time Ember breathed out, instead of a big flame — just a tiny, warm sparkle appeared.

Soon Ember's rumbles turned into soft hums. Forest animals peeked out, curious instead of scared.

"You're not scary. You're just… big and wonderful."

From that night on, the fairy and the dragon met every evening — Luma sprinkling sparkles, Ember glowing softly like a warm lantern in the dark.

The end. 🌙✨

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: The Three Big Cats and the Tiny Mouse
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
Under the silver moon, where the grasses swayed,
Three big cats prowled where the fireflies played.

A sleek spotted leopard with bright golden eyes,
A tiger with stripes like the dusk-painted skies,
And a lion with a mane like a warm golden crown
Who let out a rumble that shook the whole ground.

They were fast. They were fierce. They were proud as could be.
The three biggest hunters that jungle could see.

But one small grey mouse sat high in a tree
And watched those three big cats with curious glee.

"I wonder if they ever play?"
She scurried down and called out, "Hey!"

The lion leaned down. "Did a mouse just say 'hey' to the three of us here?"

"I did. I thought maybe we could play together a while."

"You want to play chase with us? YOU? Little mouse?"

"I'm quick," she said simply. "Just try and you'll see."

ONE — TWO — THREE!

Mouse shot off through the reeds like a little grey arrow!
Down under logs! Through root tunnels and tall waving grass —
The big cats came bounding but couldn't get past!

The lion tripped over and rolled on the ground.

Mouse sat on a mushroom and straightened her ear.
"I told you."

The big cats lay panting and laughing at last.
"That tiny grey mouse is impossibly fast!"

"Again?" asked the lion. "Again!" squeaked the mouse.

And they played till the moon slipped back under the clouds.

Right in the middle — that small mouse was found.
Curled up between all three big warm purring friends,
Sleeping soft where the moonlit savanna ends.

The end. 🌙🐆🐅🦁🐭

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: The Night Picnic Feast
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
In the warm sleepy jungle where moonflowers grew,
Lived three big cats with nothing to do.

A cheetah named Zip who was speedy and bright,
A lion named Lou with a mane fluffy-white,
And a jaguar cub called Dot with gold spots
Who always got tangled in difficult knots.

"I'm bored," said Lou. "Me too," yawned Zip.
Dot untangled her tail. "Let's eat something with style."

Zip ran to the river and brought back a fish.
Lou found a bush full of berries — delish.
Dot tumbled out of a vine with some mangoes divine.

They spread their feast on a big flat grey stone under stars and soft moonlight.

Zip ate very fast. Lou ate with big chomps.
Dot dropped her mango three times, ate it with jungle dirt, not making a sound.

"My mango had dirt," Dot said. "But I liked it."

The three big cats laughed till their sides split.

Zip curled with her tail on her nose. Lou stretched wide. Dot slept soundly in the soft moonlit pines.

Three big cats. One stone. One very good night.

The end. 🌙🐆🦁✨

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Jungle Wrestle
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
In the deep green jungle where the tall grasses grew,
Zip the cheetah and Lou the lion had nothing to do.

"I'm bored," said Zip. "Me too," said Lou.

Dot the jaguar cub came bounding along, singing a made-up and very loud song.

"Wrestling!" said Dot — and pounced directly on top of Lou's mane.

Lou blinked once. Then pounced right back. Zip watched — then jumped on them both.

And so began the Great Jungle Wrestling Match
(An event with no rules and no ribbon to catch).

Dot bit Lou's ear (gently — she had small teeth).
Lou sat on Zip (who complained from beneath).
Zip ran three laps around both of them fast,
Then flopped on top of the pile at last.

They rumbled and rolled through the tall jungle grass
Until every last bit of their boredom had passed.

Finally — panting and tangled in a heap — three big cats looked at each other.

And fell fast asleep.

The end. 🌙🐆🦁💨

steph-kids-stories-rush.title: Mama Panther and the Moonlit Hunt
steph-kids-stories-rush.body:
In the deep jungle grass where the night bugs hummed,
A mama black panther said, "Cubs, now come."

Three little cubs hurried close to her side,
Their gold eyes shining with curious pride.

There was Kiri, who crouched very low when she crept,
And Bo, who got wiggly and rarely stayed kept,
And tiny cub Luma with soft velvet feet,
Who hoped they might finally hunt their own meat.

The moon floated high through the tall shadowed trees,
And cool jungle air drifted soft on the breeze.

"Tonight," Mama whispered, "you'll follow me near.
Stay silent. Stay patient. Use eyes and ears."

Not a twig snapped. Not a leaf shook.
The panther family slipped like shadows through brook
Mist and moonlight and fern-covered ground,
Making hardly the tiniest rustling sound.

Then Mama stopped still beside tall reeds ahead.
The cubs froze quietly just as she said.

Near the riverbank under the pale silver sky,
A plump jungle rabbit hopped slowly nearby.

Mama's tail twitched once. Her shoulders went low.
The cubs watched carefully, still as stone snow.

Then — SWIFT as the wind through the dark jungle night —
Mama sprang forward in one smooth black flight.

A rustle. A leap. Then the reeds became still.
The hunt had been quick with great panther skill.

Mama carried the rabbit back over the grass
And laid it down gently where moonbeams could pass.

"This is how we eat," Mama said calm and low.
"The jungle gives food so our family can grow."

The cubs sniffed the meat with respectful small noses.
Bo sat extra still now instead of all bouncy poses.

Kiri listened closely. Luma stayed near.
The night felt important and quiet and clear.

Then side by side in the soft moonlit deep,
The panther family settled to eat.

Above them the stars shimmered bright through the trees,
While frogs croaked softly beside the dark reeds.

The end. 🌙🐆
